tweets: Kedarnath — one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, where Śiva is revered as an endless pillar of light named across the land in the Śiva Purāṇa. Its liṅga is svayambhū, self-manifest, housed in a grey-stone shrine fitted without mortar, 3,583 m up in the Himalayas.

The twelve stretch from Somnāth on Gujarat's coast to Rāmeśwaram's southern shore — a sacred geography binding the subcontinent to Śiva's light. In the 2013 floods, a boulder is said to have shielded these ancient walls. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history
